trustClaim.label: K3-TB trusted-boundary
trustClaim.summary: K3-TB trusted-boundary only; not fully formal K3 and not proven equivalent to Lean 4.

purpose: Make the formal proof roadmap explicit, auditable, and impossible to silently overclaim while the project remains K3-TB trusted-boundary.

states.open: No formal proof artifact exists yet. Engineering tests may exist, but the obligation is not proven.
states.evidence-only: Regression or audit evidence exists, but no accepted formal proof artifact exists.
states.blocked-external-lean: The obligation needs a pinned Lean executable or exported Lean artifact to check.
states.proved: A formal proof artifact exists and is checked by a required command. No P5.6 formal Lean-equivalence obligations are in this state.

obligations.title: TS K3-TB kernel accepts exactly the intended Lean-compatible Core fragment
nextProofWork: Define the Core fragment semantics formally.
Map every K3-TB kernel rule to the pinned Lean kernel/reference rule.
Replace evidence-only classifier/certificate checks with checked formal proofs.

obligations.title: Checked Core typing rules preserve type soundness for the supported fragment
nextProofWork: Prove state preservation/progress or equivalent kernel consistency theorem for the explicit Core fragment.
Prove substitution, weakening, and reduction lemmas for Core.

obligations.title: Parser/elaborator output has the same meaning as the accepted surface program
nextProofWork: Specify each elaborator lowering rule from syntax to Core.
Prove generated Core has the intended type and denotation for each supported source construct.

obligations.title: Checked bootstrap declarations faithfully implement PSC-1 primitive library semantics
nextProofWork: Formalize Nat/Bool/Eq bootstrap semantics.
Prove bootstrap artifact regeneration is deterministic and corresponds to the source.

obligations.title: TypeScript/JavaScript emission preserves observable executable Core semantics
nextProofWork: Define observable semantics for executable Core.
Prove each emitted JS/TS expression refines the Core evaluator semantics under the stated runtime assumptions.

obligations.title: Runtime helpers implement the declared executable semantics for Nat, Bool, structures, and inductives
nextProofWork: Write a formal runtime model for JavaScript/TypeScript observable values used by PSC-1.
Prove runtime helper equations match checked bootstrap equations.

obligations.title: .pscore artifacts and certificates replay to the same checked declarations
nextProofWork: Specify artifact encoding as an injective representation of Core.
Prove verifier replay is independent of parser/elaborator behavior.

obligations.title: Every supported feature records its proof/kernel/backend/runtime obligation story
nextProofWork: Require every supported feature to list proofObligationIds linked to this ledger.
Require each new kernel-impacting feature to link to a concrete formal theorem or open proof obligation.
Promote engineering evidence to formal artifacts feature by feature.

obligations.title: Supported examples are cross-checked against pinned Lean when available
nextProofWork: Pin Lean executable path and version in CI.
Expand paired ProofScript/Lean corpus for all supported PSC-1 features.

obligations.title: The trusted computing base remains small and independent of product/runtime/plugin layers
nextProofWork: Separate an independently auditable kernel/verifier release artifact.
Document exactly what must be trusted to verify a .pscore file without the compiler frontend.
